# Page Transition Accessibility Design Plan > **For Claude:** Use a11y-planner protocol. Review with a11y-critic after implementation. > **Compliance target:** WCAG 2.2 AA > **Users who need accessibility:** Screen reader users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver), keyboard-only users, vestibular motion-sensitive users, low vision users > **Assistive technologies:** NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, keyboard-only navigation, screen magnifier **Feature:** `PageTransition` wrapper component for React Router v6 routes using framer-motion **Risk Level:** Medium-High (Motion sensitivity + focus management + DOM overlap during transition) **Component/Page Type:** Route Transition Wrapper / SPA Navigation Pattern --- ## Scope & Context - **What is being built?** A route transition wrapper that animates page changes (slide 300ms, fade 200ms) using framer-motion's `AnimatePresence`. - **User need:** Smooth visual transitions between routes without breaking assistive technology, disorienting keyboard users, or violating motion preferences. - **Compliance target:** WCAG 2.2 AA - **Assistive tech requirements:** Must work with NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver (screen readers), keyboard-only navigation, and respect system-level `prefers-reduced-motion`. - **Risk factors:** - Motion-sensitive users may experience vestibular triggers from 300ms/200ms transforms. - Screen readers may read exiting page content during DOM overlap. - Focus remains on invisible/outdated elements after route change (WCAG 2.4.3 violation). - No existing motion preference detection or post-navigation focus management. - **Constraints:** framer-motion mandatory; fixed durations (300ms slide, 200ms fade); instant route change; no in-page micro-animation scope. --- ## Semantic Structure Plan The transition wrapper does not alter document structure but must preserve landmarks and heading hierarchy during animation: ```html
...
...

New Page Title

...route content...
``` - **Landmarks:** `
` and `
` remain static. The transition wrapper must NOT introduce new landmarks or break existing ones during animation. - **Heading hierarchy:** Each route must maintain its own `h1 → h2` hierarchy. The wrapper does not modify headings. - **WCAG citation:** 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (landmarks/structure preserved), 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks (skip links remain functional). --- ## Interaction Pattern Design This is a SPA route transition pattern, not a traditional interactive widget. It follows WCAG dynamic content and navigation guidelines: | Widget | APG Pattern / WCAG Reference | Keyboard Model | ARIA Attributes | WCAG Citation | |--------|------------------------------|----------------|-----------------|---------------| | Route links/buttons (trigger) | Standard Navigation Links | Tab to link, Enter/Space activates → triggers transition | None required (native semantics) | 2.1.1 Keyboard, 4.1.2 Name Role Value | | PageTransition wrapper | SPA Route Change Pattern (WCAG 2.4.3 + 2.3.3) | No custom keys; respects native link activation | `aria-hidden` on exiting page, `role="region"` optional on container | 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions, 2.4.3 Focus Order | | Route announcer | Live Region (Status) | None (passive) | `aria-live="polite"`, `role="status"` | 4.1.3 Status Messages | - **Keyboard model:** Standard React Router link/button activation triggers the transition. No custom keyboard shortcuts are added to the wrapper itself. - **Screen reader announcements:** - On focus: Screen readers announce link name/role normally. - On navigation: New page title announced via `aria-live="polite"` region. - Exiting content: Must be ignored by screen readers during transition. --- ## Focus Management Plan Post-navigation focus management is critical to prevent WCAG 2.4.3 violations (focus remains on invisible/outdated elements): 1. **Focus target:** Move focus to the `
` element or the first `

` in the new route immediately after route change completes. 2. **Technique:** Use a `useRef` attached to a dedicated focus target div inside `
`. Listen to React Router's `location.key` changes via `useEffect`. When location changes, call `focusTargetRef.current?.focus({ preventScroll: true })`. 3. **Focus restoration:** Not applicable (no modal/overlay). This is route navigation, not a dialog close. 4. **Focus indicators:** Default browser focus ring remains sufficient. Ensure no CSS in the transition wrapper overrides `:focus-visible` styles. 5. **WCAG citations:** - 2.4.3 Focus Order: Focus must move to a meaningful location on route change. - 2.1.1 Keyboard: Navigation links must remain keyboard-activatable. **Focus plan stub:** ``` Focus Management Strategy: 1. Attach ref to
inside each route's
2. useEffect listens to router location changes 3. On change: ref.current.focus({ preventScroll: true }) 4. Fallback: If focus fails, rely on browser default (top of page) but log warning 5. Verify: Screen reader announces new page title + reads from focused heading ``` --- ## State Communication Design | State | Visual Indicator | Programmatic Indicator | ARIA Attribute | WCAG Citation | |-------|-----------------|----------------------|-----------------|---------------| | Transitioning (slide/fade) | CSS transform/opacity animation | `aria-hidden="true"` on exiting page, `aria-busy` not required | `aria-hidden` on exiting wrapper | 4.1.2 Name Role Value, 4.1.3 Status Messages | | Route change complete | New content visible | Focus moves to `
`/heading, live region updates | `aria-live="polite"` on announcer | 4.1.3 Status Messages | | Reduced motion preferred | Instant switch or ≤50ms opacity fade | `useReducedMotion()` returns true, variants skip animation | None (native behavior) | 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions | - **DOM overlap handling:** `AnimatePresence` with `mode="popLayout"` keeps both pages in DOM during transition. Screen readers will read the exiting page unless explicitly hidden. Apply `aria-hidden={isExiting}` to the root element of the exiting page component. - **Route announcement:** Implement a dedicated `
` that updates with the new route's title when `location.key` changes. This ensures screen reader users are notified without visual disruption. - **WCAG citations:** 4.1.2 (state communication), 4.1.3 (dynamic updates), 2.4.3 (focus order). --- ## Visual Accessibility Plan ### Motion Reduction (WCAG 2.3.3 & SC 1.4.8) - **Detection:** Use framer-motion's `useReducedMotion()` hook to read system preference. - **Fallback strategy:** - Slide variant (300ms): Replace with instant route switch (opacity remains 1, no transform). - Fade variant (200ms): Replace with ≤50ms opacity cross-fade to maintain context without vestibular trigger. - **Implementation:** Pass `reduceMotion={useReducedMotion()}` to ``. Conditionally disable variants when reduced motion is preferred: ```js const reduceMotion = useReducedMotion(); const slideVariants = reduceMotion ? { exit: {}, enter: {} } // instant : { exit: { x: -100, opacity: 0 }, enter: { x: 100, opacity: 0 } }; ``` - **WCAG citations:** - 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions: User-controlled animations must respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. - 1.4.8 Visual Presentation: Motion preferences must be honored. ### Focus Indicators & Contrast - Default browser focus rings remain sufficient (3:1 contrast). - No custom focus styles overridden by transition wrapper CSS. - All text meets 4.5:1 normal / 3:1 large contrast ratios (unchanged from base app). --- ## Content Accessibility Plan - **Reading order:** DOM order must match visual reading order. `AnimatePresence` with `popLayout` may visually reorder during animation but DOM structure remains static. Ensure no CSS `order` or `grid-area` reordering conflicts. - **Link text quality:** Navigation links triggering transitions must have descriptive text (WCAG 2.4.4). Not modified by wrapper, but worth noting for route context. - **Language attributes:** `` remains static. Route changes do not alter language in this scope. - **Error/empty states:** If a route renders an empty state during transition, ensure it's announced via `aria-live="polite"` if applicable (outside core scope but noted). --- ## Testing Strategy ### Testing Layer Architecture - **Static analysis:** eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y catches missing `aria-hidden` or invalid ARIA in wrapper. - **Runtime scanning:** axe-core verifies landmarks, headings, and live region presence. - **Keyboard interaction testing:** Playwright real key presses verify focus movement and link activation. - **Manual screen reader testing:** NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver verify route announcements, exiting content suppression, and reading order. - **Visual regression:** DevTools `prefers-reduced-motion` toggle verifies instant/short-fade fallback. ### Test Cases 1. **Keyboard navigation:** Tab through all route links → press Enter → focus moves to new page's `
` or first heading within 300ms. 2. **Screen reader announcement:** Navigate to new route → screen reader announces new page title via `aria-live` region. 3. **DOM overlap suppression:** Inspect DOM during transition → exiting page has `aria-hidden="true"` → screen reader ignores it. 4. **Reduced motion toggle:** Enable `prefers-reduced-motion` in OS/DevTools → slide becomes instant, fade becomes ≤50ms opacity change → no transform animation plays. 5. **Focus restoration:** Navigate away from page → return via browser back button → focus lands on same meaningful location (not top of document). 6. **Contrast & zoom:** Verify focus indicators visible at 200% zoom; text remains readable during transition. ### Acceptance Criteria - Focus moves to `
` or first heading on every route change. - Screen reader announces new page title within 500ms of navigation. - Exiting page is completely ignored by screen readers during transition. - `prefers-reduced-motion` respected: no transform/opacity animations >50ms play when enabled. - No double announcements or focus loss during fast successive navigations. --- ## Implementation Tasks ### Task 1: Motion Reduction Integration 🔍 **Review checkpoint after this task** **Files:** - `components/PageTransition.tsx` - `hooks/useReducedMotion.ts` (if not using framer-motion's built-in) **Structure Stub:** ```tsx {children} ``` **ARIA Attributes:** - `reduceMotion={useReducedMotion()}` on `` (WCAG 2.3.3) - Conditional variants: instant/≤50ms when reduced motion preferred **Keyboard Interactions:** - None required for wrapper; respects native link activation **Tests:** - Verify animation stops or becomes instant when `prefers-reduced-motion` enabled - Verify no transform/opacity >50ms plays in reduced mode **WCAG Criteria:** - WCAG 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions - WCAG 1.4.8 Visual Presentation --- ### Task 2: Focus Management on Route Change 🔍 **Review checkpoint after this task** **Files:** - `components/PageTransition.tsx` - `hooks/useRouteFocus.ts` **Structure Stub:** ```tsx
{children}
``` **ARIA Attributes:** - `tabIndex="-1"` on focus target div (programmatically focusable) - No ARIA roles needed; native `
` handles landmark **Keyboard Interactions:** - `useEffect` listens to `location.key` changes - Calls `focusTargetRef.current?.focus({ preventScroll: true })` on change **Tests:** - Focus lands on target div within 300ms of navigation - Screen reader reads from focused location, not top of page - No focus loss or double-focus during rapid navigation **WCAG Criteria:** - WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order - WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard --- ### Task 3: Route Announcement Live Region 🔍 **Review checkpoint after this task** **Files:** - `components/PageTransition.tsx` - `components/RouteAnnouncer.tsx` **Structure Stub:** ```tsx
{currentRouteTitle}
``` **ARIA Attributes:** - `aria-live="polite"` (WCAG 4.1.3) - `role="status"` (equivalent to polite, explicit for clarity) - Updates with new page title on location change **Keyboard Interactions:** - None; passive live region **Tests:** - Screen reader announces new page title within 500ms - No duplicate announcements on rapid navigation - Region remains visually hidden but accessible **WCAG Criteria:** - WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages - WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (complements focus movement) --- ### Task 4: DOM Overlap Suppression 🔍 **Review checkpoint after this task** **Files:** - `components/PageTransition.tsx` - `components/RoutePageWrapper.tsx` (or inline logic) **Structure Stub:** ```tsx {children} ``` **ARIA Attributes:** - `aria-hidden={isExiting}` on exiting page wrapper (WCAG 4.1.2) - `inert` not required; `aria-hidden` sufficient for SR suppression **Keyboard Interactions:** - None; purely state-driven visibility control **Tests:** - Inspect DOM during transition → exiting page has `aria-hidden="true"` - Screen reader ignores exiting content completely - No focusable elements in exiting page receive keyboard focus **WCAG Criteria:** - WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value - WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (prevents focus on invisible content) --- ## a11y-Critic Review Checkpoints | Checkpoint | After Task | Focus Areas | |-----------|-----------|------------| | 🔍 1 | Task 1 | Verify `useReducedMotion()` correctly reads system preference, variants skip animation when reduced, no >50ms transforms play in reduced mode | | 🔍 2 | Task 2 | Verify focus moves to `
`/heading on every route change, no focus loss, `preventScroll: true` prevents jarring jumps, screen reader reads from correct location | | 🔍 3 | Task 3 | Verify `aria-live="polite"` region updates with new title, no duplicate announcements, region remains visually hidden but accessible to AT | | 🔍 4 | Task 4 | Verify `aria-hidden="true"` applied to exiting page root during transition, screen reader ignores it completely, no focusable elements remain interactive in exiting content | --- ## Contract Appendix (for spec-kitty-bridge WP translation) ### Architecture Overview Single `PageTransition` wrapper component integrating framer-motion's `AnimatePresence` with WCAG-compliant motion reduction, post-navigation focus management, route announcement live region, and DOM overlap suppression. No new interactive widgets; follows SPA navigation pattern per WCAG 2.4.3 and 2.3.3. ### Implementation Tasks #### Task 1: Motion Reduction Integration Estimated Effort: medium Depends on: none #### Test Strategy for Task 1 Verify `prefers-reduced-motion` respected; animation becomes instant or ≤50ms fade; no transform plays in reduced mode. #### Acceptance Criteria for Task 1 `useReducedMotion()` returns true when system preference enabled; variants skip animation; WCAG 2.3.3 satisfied. #### Task 2: Focus Management on Route Change Estimated Effort: medium Depends on: none #### Test Strategy for Task 2 Verify focus moves to `
`/heading on route change; screen reader reads from correct location; no focus loss. #### Acceptance Criteria for Task 2 Focus lands within 300ms of navigation; WCAG 2.4.3 satisfied; no double-focus or focus loss. #### Task 3: Route Announcement Live Region Estimated Effort: low Depends on: none #### Test Strategy for Task 3 Verify `aria-live="polite"` updates with new title; no duplicate announcements; region accessible to AT. #### Acceptance Criteria for Task 3 Screen reader announces new page title within 500ms; WCAG 4.1.3 satisfied. #### Task 4: DOM Overlap Suppression Estimated Effort: low Depends on: none #### Test Strategy for Task 4 Verify `aria-hidden="true"` on exiting page during transition; screen reader ignores it; no interactive elements remain accessible. #### Acceptance Criteria for Task 4 Exiting content fully suppressed from AT; WCAG 4.1.2 satisfied. ### Failure Modes - Motion preference ignored → vestibular trigger for sensitive users (WCAG 2.3.3) - Focus remains on invisible/outdated element → disorientation for keyboard/AT users (WCAG 2.4.3) - Screen reader reads exiting page during transition → double content, confusion (WCAG 4.1.2) - No route announcement → screen reader users unaware of page change (WCAG 4.1.3) - `aria-hidden` missing or misapplied → focusable elements remain interactive in exiting content ## References - [WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/) - [WCAG 2.2 Specification](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/quickref/) - [framer-motion useReducedMotion](https://www.framer.com/motion/use-reduced-motion/) - [React Router v6 Navigation Patterns](https://reactrouter.com/en/main) - [a11y-critic skill](https://github.com/zivtech/accessibility-skills) — for post-implementation review - [accessibility-testing skill](https://github.com/zivtech/zivtech-claude-skills) — for automated testing
